what_it_does: Modern chips used in self-driving cars or augmented-reality headsets contain many specialized processing units (for vision, AI inference, sensor fusion, etc.) that must each finish their assigned jobs before strict time deadlines — and the chip must also stay within tight power and physical-area budgets. Choosing the right mix and configuration of these units (called design space exploration) involves an astronomically large number of combinations when you also have to decide which unit runs which task at runtime. ARTEMIS shrinks this search by building a smart real-time task scheduler directly into the exploration process; because the scheduler handles task-to-hardware assignments automatically, the architect only needs to search over chip configurations, not over assignments too. The method also uses intelligent ranking rules that prioritize designs likely to meet deadlines and fit within power/area limits, and was tested on real programmable hardware (an FPGA — a chip you can reprogram) using autonomous-vehicle and AR/VR workloads.
